title: Microbe Isolation and Taxonomic Classification from Environmental Samples
author: Yiheng Hu
materials: Put the plate into Thermocycler and set it as follows: 15 mins @ 60 o C 10 mins @ 99 o C 2 mins @ 4 o C 5 mins @ 99 o C Maintaining @ 10 o C.

During the Thermocycler is running, prepare the PCR reaction MasterMix as follows (We used FirePool mastermix): 5X PCR mastermix 4 uL ITS1F/27F 0.5 uL LR6/1492R 0.5 uL Water 13 uL Make 100X mastermix and distribute 18 uL into another 96-well PCR plate (Volume might differ if using different PCR mastermix).

After spinning down the reaction, place the PCR plate on a Thermocycler and set it as the manufacturer's protocol of the PCR mastermix. Here we use ours (FIREPol 5X PCR mastermix) as an example: 5 mins @ 95 o C { 30s @ 95 o C 40s @ 56 o C 90s @ 72 o C } X 30 cycles 5 mins @ 72 o C Maintaining @ 10 o C

After spinning down the reaction, place the PCR plate on a Thermocycler and set it as the manufacturer's protocol of the polymerase. Here is our setting of Q5: 30s @ 98 o C { 10s @ 98 o C 20s @ 56 o C 40s @ 72 o C } X 33 cycles 2 mins @ 72 o C Maintaining @ 10 o C

2. Prepare all the microbe tissues together and kept in -80oC freezer for bulk extraction later. This way is more organized and time-saving, as we do not need to crush samples in liquid nitrogen every time. Generally, take 20 - 50mg tissue directly from the plate and place it in a 2mL Eppendorf tube. Freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen and add two metal balls (3mm in diameter) inside. Put all the frozen tubes in a Qiagen Tissuelyzer II and shake for 3 rounds of 30s @ 25Hz. Put tubes back to liquid nitrogen between every two rounds.

After spinning down the reaction, place the PCR plate on a Thermocycler and set it as the manufacturer's protocol of the PCR mastermix. steps.title: Prepare Buffer Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare 96-well plates with the appropriate buffer based on the target microbe.

substeps.instruction: For bacteria: add 40uL TE buffer per well.
For fungi: add 30uL 10% Chelex + 10uL TE buffer per well.

steps.title: Initial Colony Isolation
steps.instruction: Isolate single colonies from initial streaking plates onto plates with grids.

substeps.instruction: Pick single yeast or bacterial colonies from each dilution onto grid plates.
Label plates with date and experimental details (e.g., temperature, media).
Take a photo of each plate.
For filamentous fungi: cut a small square from the growing edge of each colony and place it in the middle of a small plate (5.8cm diameter).

steps.title: First Round Subculturing
steps.instruction: Incubate the first-round subcultures at 22°C for more than 2 days.

steps.title: Second Round Subculturing
steps.instruction: Re-isolate visible colonies from the large grid plates (12cm diameter) onto small plates (5.8cm diameter).

substeps.instruction: Re-streak isolates onto small plates.
Add antibiotics if necessary (e.g., for fungal isolation).
Incubate at 22°C for sub-culturing.

steps.title: Isolate Storage
steps.instruction: Monitor second-round subcultures daily starting from day 3; once isolates grow well, move them to the cold room.

steps.title: Microbe Tissue Sampling
steps.instruction: Transfer microbe tissue from small plates into the prepared 96-well buffer plates.

substeps.instruction: Use a 10uL pipette tip to pick a small amount of microbe tissue per well.
For filamentous fungi, collect mycelium only and avoid agar.
After every 12 wells (one row), press the back of the tip with a finger to push remaining buffer back into the well.
Cover the plate, vortex briefly, and spin down.

steps.title: DNA Extraction and Recovery
steps.instruction: Perform a boil-freeze-boil cycle and recover the DNA supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the DNA plate for 1 min at 2000g after the boil-freeze-boil cycle.
Use a multichannel pipette to transfer 2uL of the supernatant from each well into a corresponding PCR plate.
Seal both plates, vortex the PCR plate, and perform a quick spin.

steps.title: Colony PCR Screening
steps.instruction: Perform colony PCR and verify results via gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Run PCR products on a 1% Agarose gel to identify positive samples.

steps.title: Merge Positive DNA Samples
steps.instruction: Consolidate DNA from positive colony PCR samples into a new 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Pipette DNA from positive samples into a new 96-well plate.
Leave one well empty as an internal control for Sanger sequencing (using 95/96 wells).
Record the mapping in a 'Merged DNA plate from positive colony PCR.xlsx' file.

steps.title: High Fidelity PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Perform high-fidelity PCR using a proofreading polymerase (e.g., Q5 or Fusion).

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 50uL reaction mix: 10uL 5X Q5 buffer, 10uL High GC enhancer, 1uL dNTPs, 2.5uL ITS1F/27F, 2.5uL LR6/1492R, 0.5uL Q5, 2uL DNA, and 21.5uL Water.
Create a 96X mastermix and distribute 48uL into another 96-well PCR plate.

steps.title: PCR Product Cleanup
steps.instruction: Purify PCR products using magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.8 volume (40uL) of self-made magnetic beads to each well of a 96-well round bottom plate.
Transfer PCR products to the round bottom plate; mix for 3 mins at 1000rpm on a thermoblock at RT (or pipette up/down 10 times).
Let the plate rest covered for 5 mins.
Place on a magnetic plate for ~3 min until beads reach the edge, then remove the supernatant.
Wash each well twice with 180uL 70% ethanol using a multichannel pipette; do not re-suspend the beads.
Let the beads dry for at least 2 min until small cracks appear.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA from the magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 20uL of 10mM Tris HCl pH8 to each well.
Remove from magnet and shake on a thermoblock at RT for >20 mins at 1000 rpm.
Place on magnetic rack for 5 mins, then pipette the DNA suspension into a new 96-well plate.

steps.title: Sanger Sequencing Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the sequencing plate based on facility requirements (e.g., Eurofins Genomics).

substeps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with NanoDrop to calculate the average.
Pipette the required amount of DNA (e.g., 150ng in 15uL) into the sequencing plate.
Add 2uL 10uM primer (forward primer first) into each well.
Seal and send the plate for sequencing.

steps.title: Troubleshooting and Reverse Sequencing
steps.instruction: Perform troubleshooting for failed wells and proceed to reverse sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Check NanoDrop for failed wells.
If concentration is too high (>2x average), adjust before reverse sequencing.
If concentration is too low or quality is poor, re-run PCR using a different polymerase or original mastermix, purify, and replace the well.

steps.title: Handling Negative Colony PCR Samples
steps.instruction: For samples with negative colony PCR results, perform full DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Extract DNA from tissue using commercial column-based kits (preferred over precipitation-based).
Measure DNA concentration with NanoDrop.
Perform a PCR test with PCR Mastermix to check for marker gene amplification.
For positive samples, repeat the high-fidelity PCR and cleanup process (referencing the steps for Q5 PCR and bead cleanup).
Measure concentration and send for Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Sequence Analysis and Taxonomy
steps.instruction: Process sequencing data for taxonomic assignment.

substeps.instruction: Extract .abi files and store copies in cloud (e.g., DataPLANT) and local storage.
Perform two sequencing runs per product to avoid homopolymer errors; align the two .abi files.
Manually extract the high-quality region in fasta format.
Run BLAST against the NCBI nucleotide database to determine the species.
Generate a phylogenetic tree with all Sanger sequencing data.
